item.title: Jinko ESS Targets 1 GWh Latin America Storage Buildout as Grid Constraints Intensify - Energy News
item.description: Jinko ESS has secured a strategic cooperation agreement covering 1 GWh of battery energy storage systems across the region. The portfolio is focused on grid-side and utility-scale deployments, reflecting a broader shift in storage demand from behind-the-meter applications toward system-level balancing.

item.title: AI Data Center Capex Nears $9 Trillion as Demand Arithmetic Collides With Power, Debt, and Adoption Risk - Energy News
item.description: A revised aggregation of hyperscaler capital plans, adjusted for construction inflation and expanded private AI investment cycles, places the global AI infrastructure buildout near $9 trillion through 2030.

item.title: Italy’s €6B Hydrogen Contract-for-Difference Scheme Tests Economics of Industrial Decarbonization - Energy News
item.description: Brussels’ approval of Italy’s €6 billion ($6.9 billion) hydrogen support scheme comes at a moment when verified green hydrogen output in the country remains near industrial infancy, with production estimated at just 27 tonnes per day.

item.title: Chiyoda, NYK, and KNCC Expand CCS Ambitions as CO2 Transport Economics Remain Unsettled - Energy News
item.description: Chiyoda Corporation, Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha, and Knutsen NYK Carbon Carriers have signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly explore carbon capture and storage deployment across global markets.

item.title: Daimler Truck, Volvo, and Toyota Expand Fuel Cell Alliance - Energy News
item.description: Daimler Truck AG, Volvo Group, and Toyota Motor Corporation have signed a non-binding agreement to jointly advance fuel cell systems through their existing joint venture, cellcentric.

item.title: We’ve Been Building Fusion Reactors Wrong for 70 Years - Energy News
item.description: Fusion energy systems have spent decades operating under a persistent commercial constraint: even advanced experimental reactors still struggle with net energy stability once internal power demands are fully accounted for.

item.title: Rolls-Royce Expands Energy Storage Portfolio with 86 MWh UK Grid Project - Energy News
item.description: Rolls-Royce has begun construction of its first large-scale battery energy storage system in the domestic market, signaling a strategic shift from global deployments toward participation in one of Europe’s most advanced storage ecosystems.

item.title: Kansas Counties Stall Battery Storage Buildout as Regulatory Gaps Trigger Moratoriums - Energy News
item.description: The Sedgwick County Commission approved a moratorium on new battery energy storage system applications through March 11, 2027. The decision reflects a widening disconnect between the pace of grid-scale storage deployment and the readiness of local governance structures to evaluate and regulate these projects.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz Disruption Cuts LNG Capacity by Up to 87 bcm, Driving Price Shock Scenarios Across Global Gas Markets - Energy News
item.description: Global LNG markets are operating under an extreme stress test as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz collapses from an average of 94 vessels per day to just over five in early March 2026, with LNG and oil tanker flows falling from more than 53 per day to roughly two.

item.title: Lhyfe Revenue Doubles but Losses Deepen as Green Hydrogen Scaling Costs Outpace Market Growth - Energy News
item.description: Revenue growth in Europe’s green hydrogen sector continues to lag behind capital intensity, with Paris-listed Lhyfe reporting a near doubling of annual revenue to approximately €10 million in 2025 while posting a net loss of €51 million, up sharply from €29.2 million a year earlier.
